subsystems.name: Deposition system
subsystems.role: moves the print head and deposits material layer by layer to form the structure.

subsystems.name: Material supply and mixing
subsystems.role: prepares and delivers the advanced material to the print head at a controlled rate.

subsystems.name: Printing material
subsystems.role: the advanced polymer, metal or concrete that forms the load-bearing structure.

subsystems.name: Reinforcement integration
subsystems.role: adds tensile strength to printed elements, which are often weak in tension.

subsystems.name: Control and design software
subsystems.role: translates designs into toolpaths and monitors the build in real time.

subsystems.name: Post-processing and assembly
subsystems.role: finishes printed components and joins them into larger structures.

buildSteps.title: Design and simulate
buildSteps.detail: Create a digital model of the structure, simulate loads and generate the printing paths layer by layer.

buildSteps.title: Prepare material
buildSteps.detail: Mix and condition the advanced material — concrete with admixtures, metal wire, or polymer pellets — for consistent flow.

buildSteps.title: Set up printing system
buildSteps.detail: Erect the gantry or position robotic arms around the build site and calibrate the deposition head.

buildSteps.title: Deposit layers
buildSteps.detail: The print head extrudes material in precise paths, building up the structure one layer at a time.

buildSteps.title: Integrate reinforcement
buildSteps.detail: During printing, place steel cables, mesh or tendons either manually or robotically to carry tensile loads.

buildSteps.title: Monitor and correct
buildSteps.detail: Use sensors to detect voids, slumps or misalignment and adjust flow, speed and path in real time.

buildSteps.title: Cure and finish
buildSteps.detail: Allow the material to cure or solidify, then machine surfaces and add connection details.

buildSteps.title: Assemble and inspect
buildSteps.detail: If built off-site, transport and join printed sections using robotic welding or bonding, then inspect structural integrity.

prerequisites.why: concrete printing has built houses and bridges, but rates and scales remain far below civilisational projects.
high-performance concrete and printable metal alloys exist, but they are not yet optimised for large-scale freeform printing.
no established method continuously reinforces large printed elements, which limits their use in load-bearing megastructures.
sensors and algorithms are emerging for small builds but are not proven over hundreds of metres.
building codes do not yet cover additive construction, blocking certification of critical infrastructure.

pathway.milestone: 3D-printed houses and a steel bridge in Amsterdam demonstrate the concept
pathway.unlocks: confidence in materials and processes for small-scale construction.

pathway.milestone: commercial printing of building components and bridge spans
pathway.unlocks: lower cost, less waste and faster construction for standard projects.

pathway.milestone: on-site printing of entire buildings with integrated reinforcement
pathway.unlocks: rapid construction in remote, hazardous or resource-scarce locations.

pathway.milestone: civilisation-scale megastructures such as dams, towers or space habitats
pathway.unlocks: construction beyond the limits of conventional labour and logistics.
